note: Every project closes capabilities marked solo. Nothing here claims to close on-call, production incidents, compliance or any other capability that needs a real organisation.

projects.title: Build a small warehouse from a public API and publish the model behind it
projects.artifact: A loaded warehouse, the dbt project that builds it, and a data dictionary explaining every column
projects.dataSource: Any public API with a real entity model, pulled on a schedule so the history is yours

projects.title: Add data quality gates to a pipeline and show what they caught
projects.artifact: A pipeline with failing and passing checks, plus a written log of real defects the gates caught
projects.dataSource: A messy public dataset, ideally one that updates, so the checks fire on genuinely new problems

projects.title: Build a streaming pipeline over a live public feed
projects.artifact: A running consumer, a replayable event log, and a dashboard of lag and throughput
projects.dataSource: A public websocket or polling feed that emits continuously, so backpressure is real rather than simulated

projects.title: Answer one contested question with a dashboard someone could act on
projects.artifact: A dashboard, the query layer under it, and a written recommendation with its uncertainty stated
projects.dataSource: A public dataset where the answer is genuinely arguable, not one where the chart is obvious

projects.title: Deploy a real service to the cloud with nothing done by hand
projects.artifact: A repository that stands the whole environment up from empty, and tears it down again
projects.dataSource: Your own small service. A free tier is enough; the point is that no step is manual

projects.title: Make one service observably reliable and prove the number
projects.artifact: Dashboards, an alert that has actually fired, a stated SLO, and the load test that justifies it
projects.dataSource: A service you deployed, put under synthetic load you generate yourself

projects.title: Build the small tool that removes a chore you actually have
capabilities: Write production code in a general purpose language
projects.artifact: A published tool with a readme, tests, and a note on the time it saves per week
projects.dataSource: A repetitive task in your own workflow, timed before and after

projects.title: Design an API someone else could build against, then build it
capabilities: Write production code in a general purpose language
projects.artifact: A design document written before the code, the OpenAPI spec, and the running service
projects.dataSource: A domain you know well enough to argue about the edge cases

projects.title: Take something slow and make it fast, with the numbers either side
capabilities: Refactor and pay down technical debt
Write production code in a general purpose language
projects.artifact: A benchmark harness, a profile before and after, and a write-up of what the bottleneck really was
projects.dataSource: A slow query or script you can measure honestly, ideally in an open source project

projects.title: Refactor one real module and write down why you left the rest alone
capabilities: Refactor and pay down technical debt
projects.artifact: A branch with the refactor, the tests that make it safe, and a note on the debt you chose not to pay
projects.dataSource: A real open source repository, where the existing code is not yours to excuse

projects.title: Build a test suite for a project that has none
projects.artifact: A suite running in CI, a coverage number, and the bugs it found on the way in
projects.dataSource: An open source project with thin tests. The maintainers will tell you if the tests are wrong

projects.title: Break a real application on purpose and write the reports properly
projects.artifact: A charter-based test session log and a set of reproducible defect reports with severity reasoning
projects.dataSource: Any public beta or open source application that accepts issues

projects.title: Train a model on public data and report what it cannot do
capabilities: Train and evaluate machine learning models
projects.artifact: A notebook, a held-out evaluation, and an honest section on where the model fails
projects.dataSource: A public dataset with a real outcome variable and a defensible train and test split

projects.title: Put a model behind an API and watch it drift
capabilities: Deploy and monitor models in production
projects.artifact: A served model, a drift dashboard, and the alert that fires when inputs move
projects.dataSource: Your own trained model, fed live or replayed data so drift is real

projects.title: Build retrieval over your own documents and measure whether it helps
capabilities: Work with LLMs and applied AI
projects.artifact: A working retrieval system plus an evaluation set you wrote, with results against a no-retrieval baseline
projects.dataSource: A document collection you know well enough to judge the answers

projects.title: Threat model a real open source application
projects.artifact: A data flow diagram, a STRIDE table, and a ranked list of what you would fix first
projects.dataSource: An open source application whose source you can actually read

projects.title: Build authentication properly and write down the attacks it stops
capabilities: Write production code in a general purpose language
projects.artifact: A working sign-in flow with sessions and roles, and a document mapping each control to the attack it blocks
projects.dataSource: Your own application. The value is in the written reasoning, not the login box

projects.title: Make one component survive ten times its traffic
projects.artifact: A load test that breaks it, the change that fixes it, and the test re-run at ten times the load
projects.dataSource: A service you built, pushed until it fails, with the failure mode written down
